title.narrative: ROAP/VIE04/S1-836/Emergency support to post-disaster recovery and rehabilitation of mountainous communities in Son La Province, Viet Nam

description.narrative: This project aims to deliver immediate response and recovery support to the climate-vulnerable communities of Thuan Chau and Mai Son Districts, Son La Province, who were severely affected by Typhoon No. 2 (international name: Prapiroon), struck the northern mountainous Viet Nam in late July and beginning of August 2024. The project will enhance resilience by future-proofing infrastructure, promote sustainable development through environmental conservation, improve disaster preparedness and response, and reduce multi-dimensional poverty by improving access to basic services. The most marginalized, particularly women, people with disabilities and the poorest communities will be placed at the heart of all processes to ensure a human rights-based approach to the recovery and rehabilitation. This approach will address structural inequalities and barriers that disproportionately affect these groups, securing equitable opportunities to “build back better” for everyone by fostering inclusive economic growth, social protection, accessibility, and gender-responsive policies. The project has three expected main outputs: 1. Improved protective infrastructure for early warning and immediate response 2. Enhanced ecosystem functions for disaster risk reduction 3. Strengthened disaster preparedness for effective response at all levels The project is designed with a comprehensive approach combining both hard- and soft interventions. Output 1 and Output 2 will provide tangible results to support the emergency response post-disaster, as well as prepare the communities, including those most at risk of being left behind, such as women and girls, older persons, persons with disabilities and ethnic minorities (especially in low-income and extreme poverty communities), for future disaster-related uncertainties. Hard interventions for the built environment include retrofitting/ constructing of disaster-resilient community centres with sustainable energy and water supply and installation of an integrated system for real-time flash flood and landslide forecasting/modelling. Ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction (Eco-DRR) strategy will be applied to restore and reinforce the denuded lands, aiming to enhance natural retention capacity and mitigate erosion and landslide risks. Output 3 focuses on enhancing disaster preparedness at all levels. Through UN-Habitat’s people process, the communities in their diversity, including women and girls and those at risk of exclusion, will be involved in all activities, from risk assessment and mapping, capacity building and awareness raising to integrated community planning for disaster risk reduction and climate change response. Main Expected Accomplishment: Enhanced institutional capacity and community resilience against natural hazards, especially flash floods and landslides, through gender-responsive, integrated community planning, ecosystem-based DRR and resilient infrastructure.
